item.title: Nasdaq to Kick Off Tiny Companies Faster After SEC Approves Rule
item.description: Nasdaq Inc. will change its rules to make it easier to kick off flailing businesses as regulators zero in on wild market swings and allegations of manipulation that have plagued trading in so-called microcap stocks.

item.title: Uber Cuts 10% of Customer Service Jobs, Citing ‘Embrace’ of AI
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. said it has cut 10% of jobs within its customer service operations as part of a broader effort to simplify its ranks and “embrace artificial intelligence.”

item.title: Gold Holds Gain as Dip-Buying Counters Inflation Fears From War
item.description: Gold held gains on dip-buying even as hostilities in the Middle East pushed oil prices to multiweek highs, rekindling concerns that US inflationary pressure could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: Hong Kong’s Offshore Yuan Market Evolves Into Global Funding Hub
item.description: A record pile of yuan in Hong Kong is making its way to corporate loans while driving a surge in capital market activity, signaling that China’s drive to internationalize its currency is advancing.

item.title: South Korea’s Economy Beats Estimates as Chip Boom Continues
item.description: South Korea’s economy grew faster than expected in the second quarter, driven by an artificial intelligence-fueled chip boom that supports the case for further interest-rate increases.

item.title: Coinbase to Expand Singapore Team Amid Global Restructuring: BT
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global Inc. is looking to expand its headcount in Singapore to 200 by the end of the year, up from 150, the Business Times reported Wednesday.

item.title: Musk Says Micron Gave Tesla ‘Significant’ Supply of Memory Chips
item.description: Micron Technology Inc. recently gave Tesla Inc. a “significant allocation” of memory chips, according to Elon Musk, helping meet the automaker’s demand for an increasingly precious commodity.

item.title: Amazon Investigated Over Chinese Influence by US Senate Panel
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. is being investigated by the Senate Small Business Committee for allegedly letting China influence the company’s online marketplace, according to a document reviewed by Bloomberg and two people interviewed as part of the investigation.

item.title: US Stock Futures Slip on Alphabet, Oil Advances: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures declined after Alphabet Inc.’s spending plans intensified concerns about the payoff from the industry’s aggressive artificial intelligence buildout. Oil extended its rally.

item.title: Wall Street Banks Trading Parts of $35 Billion AI Chip Deal
item.description: Wall Street banks have started buying and selling an initial piece of a $35 billion financing package for Broadcom Inc. and Anthropic PBC’s AI infrastructure expansion, with the biggest private credit deal ever now being offered to a wider pool of investors.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 23
item.description: Oil gained after Iran-backed Houthi militants said they targeted two Saudi Arabian tankers in the Red Sea, escalating the Middle East conflict and threatening deeper supply disruptions.

item.title: Samsung’s $400,000 Bonus Fuels Labor Disputes Across South Korea
item.description: Labor unions are rallying across South Korea after Samsung Electronics Co. caved in to protests and agreed to hand out bonuses of more than $400,000 to some of its employees.

item.title: Brent Crude Spikes in Late Trading After Red Sea Tanker Attack
item.description: Oil prices rose sharply in post-settlement trading Wednesday, with Brent crude oil rising near $95 a barrel after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they struck two Saudi tankers.

item.title: Google Boosts 2026 Spending Estimate to as Much as $205 Billion
item.description: Alphabet Inc. projected full-year capital expenditures will be $195 billion to $205 billion in 2026, increasing its already sky-high spending estimate for the year as it works to secure an edge in the artificial intelligence race.

item.title: Vitamin Well Raises $2.2 Billion From Cross-Currency Loan Deal
item.description: Vitamin Well AB raised about $2.2 billion through a cross-currency loan offering to fund its acquisition of protein-bar maker EMPWR Nutrition Group.

item.title: Daiwa AM Boosts Staff in Shift Toward Institutional Investors
item.description: Daiwa Asset Management Co. is planning to double its sales staff targeting institutional investors to about 20 people, its president said.

item.title: AI Mania to Fuel Australia Deals, Top Underwriter Macquarie Says
item.description: The investor demand for exposure to companies along the artificial intelligence supply chain is set to accelerate capital-market activity in Australia, according to the nation’s top dealmaker.

item.title: Google Says Cloud Services Backlog Expands to $514 Billion
item.description: Alphabet Inc. said its cloud computing unit had a $514 billion backlog of contracted work that hasn’t been recorded as revenue yet, signaling robust demand for its services that underpin the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Alphabet Posts $98 Billion in Second-Quarter Investment Gains
item.description: Alphabet Inc. on Wednesday reported investment gains of $98 billion as part of its second-quarter earnings results.

item.title: Mexico City Pozole Chain Casa de Tono Explores Sale on Expansion Pitch
item.description: Mexican family-owned restaurant chain La Casa de Toño is seeking a sale in a deal that could top $400 million and set the business up for expansion, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Southwest Hedges Full-Year Guidance as Fuel Expenses Tick Up
item.description: Southwest Airlines Co. broadened its guidance for full-year 2026 to account for uncertainty resulting from the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran, which sent fuel expenses higher in the second quarter.

item.title: Democrats Threaten Yale With Tax If School Makes Deal With Trump
item.description: A group of Democratic legislators in Connecticut with degrees from Yale University are threatening the school’s tax-exempt status if leaders make a deal with the Trump administration over probes into admission practices.

item.title: ServiceNow Posts Strong Sales and Bookings, Touts AI Strength
item.description: ServiceNow Inc. reported better-than-expected quarterly sales and bookings, boosting Wall Street’s hopes that the software maker’s new artificial intelligence tools will spur growth.

item.title: Cable One Faces 12% Yield to Fund Buyout After Debt Swap Stalls
item.description: Cable One Inc. is facing a steep cost to finalize the buyout of a company whose debt it has indicated it may not support when it comes due next year.

item.title: IBM Cuts Full-Year Sales Outlook as Mainframe Demand Drops
item.description: International Business Machines Corp. cut its full-year sales outlook, including for its closely watched software unit, after reporting a dip in demand for its mainframe business.

item.title: Texas Instruments Gets Lukewarm Reaction to Upbeat Forecast
item.description: Texas Instruments Inc., the biggest maker of analog and embedded processing chips, gave a sales forecast that topped estimates but failed to excite investors, who have bid up the company’s shares this year.

item.title: Alphabet Posts Cloud Sales Beat, Slight Miss on Search Revenue
item.description: Alphabet Inc. reported second-quarter cloud revenue that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations but slightly missed on sales tied to its search-engine business, threatening to fuel concerns about its heavy spending on artificial intelligence.

item.title: Pool Supplier Leslie’s Considers Potential Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
item.description: Pool supplier Leslie’s Inc. is considering a range of strategic options to address its debt load, including a potential Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Brazil Unveils New Relief for Companies Hit by US Tariffs
item.description: Brazil’s government unveiled a relief package worth 18.5 billion reais ($3.7 billion) in credit for exporters hit by new US tariffs, as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva seeks to shield key sectors from damage ahead of October elections.

item.title: OpenAI President Says Kimi K3 ‘Pretty Good,’ Unsure If Distilled
item.description: OpenAI President Greg Brockman acknowledged that Moonshot AI had developed a competitive new artificial intelligence model and said he wasn’t sure whether the Chinese firm had piggybacked on the ChatGPT maker’s technology.
